stemBlocks.value: A hiker follows the route OABC shown on the coordinate grid: 6 km east from O to A, 8 km north from A to B, then 3 km west from B to C. (a) Write the total displacement from O to C as a column vector, taking east and north as positive.
Think first: Displacement depends only on where you start and where you finish, not on the path taken.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p184-q11 from workbook page 184.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write each leg as a column vector.

contentBlocks.value: 6 km east = (6, 0); 8 km north = (0, 8); 3 km west = (−3, 0)
C is plotted at (3, 8), which matches the displacement from the origin

strategyBlocks.value: Write each leg as a column vector using the sign convention, then add the three vectors component by component.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) The total displacement from O to C is the column vector with components 3 and 8, that is 3 km east and 8 km north.

whyThisWorks.value: Because west is the opposite of east, the 3 km west leg simply subtracts from the eastward total — the sign convention does the work automatically. Displacement is a vector, so the three legs combine nose to tail into one resultant that depends only on the endpoints; the hiker actually walked 6 + 8 + 3 = 17 km, but ended up displaced by a vector of magnitude √(9 + 64) = √73 ≈ 8.54 km.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding the distances to get 17 and calling that the displacement.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding the distances to get 17 and calling that the displacement.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the west leg as (3, 0) and getting (9, 8).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the west leg as (3, 0) and getting (9, 8).

commonErrors.misconception: Putting the north component on top and the east component below.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Putting the north component on top and the east component below.

examTip.value: Convert every compass instruction into a signed column vector before adding — north and east positive, south and west negative — and the arithmetic takes care of itself.
